newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY K&H SEES THREE BIDDERS FOR FOUR CAN FIRMS.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY K&H SEES THREE BIDDERS FOR FOUR CAN FIRMS.

text.p: Hungary's Kereskedelmi Bank group (K&H) said on Wednesday that the planned sale of its four canned food companies attracted the interest of at least three foreign investors.
"Each of the investors would buy all the four companies," K&H CEU Janos Eros told a news conference.
He added that the potential buyers include a foreign investor, which is already present in Hungary, and two or three other foreign investors appeared to be interested in the sale.
"The lowest price about which we speak is 150 percent (of the face value)," he added.
K&H declined to disclose the total amount of the canned food companies' registered capital.
The companies are EKO, Arany Facan, SZEKO and Nagyatadi Konzervgyar, a K&H official said.

The four companies posted a total pre-tax profit of 200 nillion forints in 1995 on sales of 12 billion forints, K&H officials said, adding that the pre-tax profit was likely to increase to 500 to 600 million forints in 1996 on sales of 17 billion.
K&H, Hungary's third largest commercial bank, is spated for privatisation.
